summary: The עַכְשׁוּב occurs once, in a comparison with a serpent whose venom lies under the wicked’s lips (Psa 140:4). Paul quotes the line with Greek ἀσπίς, “asp” (Rom 3:13). The word’s origin is uncertain; its own consonants give this entry its key, without assigning it to עכר.

words.summary: The word occurs only in Psa 140:4. Its formation and any connection with עַכָּבִישׁ, “spider”, remain uncertain.

senses.definition: A creature with venom, set in parallel with the serpent, as a picture of wicked men’s tongues.

evidence.note: “They sharpen their tongue like a serpent (נָחָשׁ); the venom of an עַכְשׁוּב is under their lips.”
Paul quotes the line, “the poison of asps (ἀσπίδων) is under their lips”, among the verses showing that all are under sin.
ἰὸς ἀσπίδων ὑπὸ τὰ χείλη αὐτῶν, quoting Psa 140:4.

parallels.note: The serpent, beside the עַכְשׁוּב, for the tongue of the wicked.

note: Filed separately from עכר because no evidence derives עַכְשׁוּב from that root. The key עכשב represents the word's consonants without the vowel letter ו; it is not a reconstructed verbal root. BDB p.cq.ae files the word in its עכר section without deriving it from עכר. Possible comparison with עַכָּבִישׁ 'spider' by metathesis remains conjectural; Arabic ʿankabūt 'spider' (Lane p. 2177, root عنكب) has not been established as a cognate. The Greek ἀσπίς is the Septuagint rendering and Paul's wording in Rom 3:13.
